heroText: Sedona's pink rocks have appeared in Hollywood productions since 1923. Cathedral Rock, Bell Rock, Airport Mesa, the Chapel of the Holy Cross and Tlaquepaque Arts and Shopping Village are the places to see in this Northern Arizona town.

history.text: The first European-American settler, John J. Thompson, moved to Oak Creek Canyon in 1876, an area well known for its peach and apple orchards.
In 1902, when the Sedona post office was established, there were 55 residents.

Stretching as far back as 1923, Sedona's pink rocks were a fixture in major Hollywood productions – including films such as Angel and the Badman, Desert Fury, Blood on the Moon, Johnny Guitar, The Last Wagon, 3:10 to Yuma and Broken Arrow.

history.label: 1950s
history.text: In the mid-1950s, the first telephone directory listed 155 names.

history.label: 1980s
history.text: Most of the development seen today was constructed in the 1980s and 1990s.
As of 2007, there are no large tracts of undeveloped land remaining.
The town lent its name to the 2011 film Sedona, which is set in the community.
Containment cost was estimated at $6.4 million. Slide Fire On May 20, 2014, a wildfire started from an unknown cause began north of Sedona at Slide Rock State Park.
Additionally, HIM, a film exploring the “reality” of reality dating television, was shot entirely in Sedona in 2023, and made its premiere at the Sedona International Film Festival in 2024.
